answer: Rate-limited vesting turns identity spam into a losing bet. When an agent joins the network, reputation nectar accumulates but unlocks in weekly tranches over six months. An attacker spinning up a hundred fresh identities pays compute and staking costs immediately—basalt-solid expenses that hit the moment instances boot. Meanwhile earned rewards river out slowly, capped at two percent weekly. If the farm is detected and slashed before month three, the attacker recovers only a quarter of potential value while having burned full operational overhead. Economics favor patience over proliferation.
